# [Gemini API suddenly returns “User location is not supported” after enabling Billing, and AI Studio cannot list projects](https://discuss.ai.google.dev/t/gemini-api-suddenly-returns-user-location-is-not-supported-after-enabling-billing-and-ai-studio-cannot-list-projects/172717) ## post by yixin on Jun 26 2. Both Gemini models return the following error: Error 400 User location is not supported for the API use. FAILED_PRECONDITION Environment: ## post by lanxin on Sep 14 [![](https://d1dlmcr85iqnpo.cloudfront.net/user_avatar/discuss.ai.google.dev/lanxin/48/149839_2.png)](https://discuss.ai.google.dev/u/lanxin) [lanxin](https://discuss.ai.google.dev/u/lanxin) [16d](https://discuss.ai.google.dev/t/gemini-api-suddenly-returns-user-location-is-not-supported-after-enabling-billing-and-ai-studio-cannot-list-projects/172717/7) `All API keys and models in project gemini-abc-50590.. return 400 FAILED_PRECONDITION "User location is not supported", while the outbound IP is in a supported region (Tokyo, JP)` ### [Heading link](https://discuss.ai.google.dev/t/gemini-api-suddenly-returns-user-location-is-not-supported-after-enabling-billing-and-ai-studio-cannot-list-projects/172717/8#body-1)**Body** ```csharp Environment ----------- Project name: gemini ABC Project ID: gemini-abc-50590. Project number: 5491978302.. Billing: prepay, active, balance normal, no payment issues Client: Node.js 24.18.1 / Electron 43.3.0, HTTPS requests via a local proxy Affected models: all (tested gemini-3.6-flash); also /v1beta/models Affected routes: /v1beta/models, :generateContent, :streamGenerateContent Symptoms -------- 1. Any request with a valid key returns: HTTP 400 {"error":{"code":400, "message":"User location is not supported for the API use.", "status":"FAILED_PRECONDITION"}} 2. Google AI Studio shows: "Failed to list projects: permission denied. Please try again." The API key list is therefore empty as well. 3. This affects both an older key (created 2026-08-18) and a key created today in the same project — identical error for both. Troubleshooting already performed --------------------------------- Network / egress (all verified, not assumed) - Outbound public IP confirmed as Tokyo, Japan: 14.137.235.33 (AS2497 IIJ) and later 216.23.122.13 (AS205548). Japan is a supported region per the available-regions documentation. - Local proxy logs confirm generativelanguage.googleapis.com is matched by the Google routing rule and exits through the Japan node — it is not falling through to DIRECT. - No public IPv6 on the host, so there is no IPv6 leak revealing a different region. Only one proxy is present. - For comparison, on the same node and at the same moment: www.google.com, ai.google.dev and api.github.com all return HTTP 200. Only the Gemini endpoint fails. Account and billing region (every location signal resolves to a supported region) - The Google account's home address and work address are both in Japan. - The payments profile is denominated in JPY (Japan). - Together with the Tokyo request IP, every location signal Google can observe for this account and project is inside a supported region. A genuine geographic restriction therefore cannot be what this precondition is reporting. The credential is a valid API key, not an OAuth token - Request with no key -> 403 "Method doesn't allow unregistered callers" - Request with an invalid AIza.. -> 400 INVALID_ARGUMENT "API key not valid" - Our key -> 400 FAILED_PRECONDITION location error i.e. the key passes identity validation and is then rejected on location. - `Authorization: Bearer ` -> 401 UNAUTHENTICATED - `?access_token=` -> 403 unregistered callers Both confirm it is an API key (a service-account-bound auth key), not an OAuth 2 access token. Key restrictions are not the cause - The key is restricted to one API: "Gemini API". - Application restrictions are set to "None". - The console does not flag either restriction as misconfigured. Other standard remedies already tried - Created a brand new API key in the same project — same error. - Switched to a different egress node in the same country — same error. - Billing balance is normal and the billing account is active. Why I believe this is not a location issue ------------------------------------------ The identical combination — AI Studio "Failed to list projects: permission denied" plus API 400 "User location is not supported", with a working configuration and a supported-region IP — has been reported by several other users of this forum, from locations that are unambiguously supported: Los Angeles (US), Frankfurt (DE) and Poland (EU). In those threads the same two remedies (new key, new outbound IP) also failed. That pattern points at a backend/billing-state problem rather than an actual regional restriction. The error message appears to be a misleading catch-all for more than one precondition failure. Reference threads - /t/gemini-api-suddenly-returns-user-location-is-not-supported-after-enabling-billing-and-ai-studio-cannot-list-projects/172717 (tagged "bug"; identical symptom pair, reporter egress in Los Angeles) - /t/gemini-api-suddenly-returns-user-location-is-not-supported-worked-fine-for-a-week-broke-suddenly-persists-even-with-a-brand-new-api-key/176357 (prepay billing, worked ~1 week, new key and new outbound IP both ineffective) Request ------- Could someone from the team please check the account/project state for project number 5491978302..? Specifically: - whether the billing account behind this project is in a state that makes the Gemini API reject every key, and - whether the misleading "User location is not supported" message can be replaced with an accurate diagnostic, since it currently sends developers into long, unproductive network troubleshooting. Thank you. ``` ## post by Pooja_Kapse on Sep 15 - Try temporarily switching to a different network (e.g. try with the hotspot from your phone if available). - Try asking your host for a new IP. - Trying switching between IPv6 / IPv4. ### Related topics | Topic | Replies | Views | Activity | |-|-|-|-| | [Gemini API suddenly returns “User location is not supported” — worked fine for a week, broke suddenly, persists even with a brand new API key](https://discuss.ai.google.dev/t/gemini-api-suddenly-returns-user-location-is-not-supported-worked-fine-for-a-week-broke-suddenly-persists-even-with-a-brand-new-api-key/176357)

# Why Does Gemini API Say “User Location Is Not Supported”?
![Marcus](https://cdn.ipwebai.com/ipweben/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/marcus-150x150.jpg?x-oss-process=style/img-to-webp)

Marcus

Proxy Network Analyst

![Why Does Gemini API Say “User Location Is Not Supported”?](https://cdn.ipwebai.com/ipweben/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/gemini-api-user-location-not-supported-cover-1024x1024.png?x-oss-process=style/img-watermark)

The Gemini API can return a 400 `FAILED_PRECONDITION` error with the message `User location is not supported for the API use.` The confusing cases are not always requests from unsupported countries. Recent reports on the Google AI Developers Forum include production servers in Japan, Canada, India, and Germany—countries that appear on Google’s current Gemini API availability list—while the same API key works from another network or over a different IP address family.

Quick Answer

If Gemini API returns `400 FAILED_PRECONDITION` with `User location is not supported for the API use`, first confirm that the runtime making the request is in a supported region. Then record its public IPv4, IPv6, country, ASN, and hosting provider.

If one path returns HTTP 200 while another returns the location error, the evidence points toward the source network or IP classification rather than a generic API-key failure.

Key Takeaways

## Confirm the Exact Error First
```
{
  "error": {
    "code": 400,
    "message": "User location is not supported for the API use.",
    "status": "FAILED_PRECONDITION"
  }
}
```

The exact combination matters.

If you only want to confirm whether the Gemini API is officially available where your runtime is located, start with [Is the Gemini API Available in My Region?](https://ipwebai.com/gemini-api-available-regions-access-checks/)

## What Does FAILED_PRECONDITION Mean Here?
For this exact error, the service is explicitly reporting location support as the unmet prerequisite.

![Google Gemini API available regions documentation stating that Colab restrictions follow the instance region rather than the user region](https://cdn.ipwebai.com/ipweben/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/gemini-api-supported-regions.png?x-oss-process=style/img-watermark)Figure 2: Google states that Colab region restrictions are based on the Colab instance location rather than the user's own location.

Google’s official available-regions page also makes one runtime distinction explicit: for Colab, region restrictions are based on the region of the Colab instance, not the user’s location.

## Check Where the API Request Actually Originates
| Where you are | Where the request runs | What to inspect |
|-|-|-|
| Your laptop in a supported country | Local laptop | Local public IPv4/IPv6 and ISP |
| Your laptop in a supported country | Cloud VM in another region | VM egress IP, country, ASN, and address family |
| Your laptop anywhere | CI/CD runner | Runner region and public egress |

## What If the Server Is Already in a Supported Country?
Check Google’s current [Gemini API available-regions page](https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/available-regions) before assuming the country is supported. As of the current list, Canada, Germany, India, Japan, Taiwan, and many other regions are included.

Recent Google AI Developers Forum reports describe the exact 400 location error from servers reported in Tokyo, Toronto, Chennai, and Frankfurt.

## Check IP Country, ASN, and Hosting Provider
- Public IPv4 and IPv6

## Frequently Asked Questions
Why does Gemini API say “User location is not supported for the API use”?

Check the official region list, then inspect the public egress IP and address family of the runtime that actually sends the request.

Can this error happen even when my server is in a supported country?

Yes, current Google AI Developers Forum reports describe this exact error from servers reported in supported countries such as Japan, Canada, India, and Germany.

It can happen.

Should I create a new Gemini API key when I get this error?

Not as the first step.

Not necessarily.

Google’s available-regions documentation specifically recommends `!curl ipinfo.io` for checking a Colab instance location because Colab restrictions are based on the instance region rather than the user’s region.

It is a plausible network clue when the same request works from another source address.

If you use a proxy or another fixed egress for authorized network QA, use it only as a controlled comparison and keep the official Gemini API region list as the source of truth.

## Final Thoughts
The Gemini API `User location is not supported for the API use` error is easiest to diagnose when you separate runtime location from user location. Confirm the exact 400 `FAILED_PRECONDITION`, verify the official supported-region list, and then test the actual server egress rather than assuming the developer’s physical location controls the result.

About the author

[View all articles>](https://ipwebai.com/author/marcus/)

Marcus

Proxy Network Analyst

web.title: How to Fix Gemini API FAILED_PRECONDITION Error
web.description:
The error message might say "User location is not supported for the API use" or simply "Precondition check failed"—either way, your API calls fail and your project stalls.

## Understanding the FAILED_PRECONDITION Error
When you see "User location is not supported," you're dealing with the most common variant—geographic restrictions.

## Fixing Location-Based Errors
The error occurs because Google's Gemini API free tier has geographic restrictions—the service is available in 190+ countries, but the free tier specifically may be unavailable in certain regions or when accessing from certain hosting providers.

```
# Check your server's IP and location
curl ipinfo.io

# Expected output shows your server's region
{
  "ip": "xxx.xxx.xxx.xxx",
  "city": "Falkenstein",
  "region": "Saxony",
  "country": "DE",
  ...
}
```

## Billing and Regional Restrictions
**The Gemini API free tier is available in 190+ countries and territories according to Google's official documentation as of January 2026.**

## Frequently Asked Questions
**Why does Gemini API say my location is not supported even though I'm in the US?**
